subject: Biotechnology
title: Agrobacterium: Nature's Engineer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Agrobacterium: Nature's Engineer.

hook.text: A soil bacterium naturally inserts its DNA into plant cells — scientists hijacked this trick to create GMO crops.

buildup.text: Agrobacterium tumefaciens causes crown gall disease — its Ti plasmid transfers T-DNA into plant chromosomes.

discovery.text: Replace the tumor genes with useful ones — the bacterium still delivers, but now it brings gifts instead of disease.

twist.text: Agrobacterium works mainly on dicots — cereals like rice and corn needed gene guns or modified protocols.

climax.text: Most transgenic crops today were created using Agrobacterium — nature's genetic engineer, domesticated by humans.

punchline.text: A bacterium that edits plants naturally — we just changed what it delivers.

quiz.question: How does Agrobacterium transfer genes into plant cells?
options: It injects proteins that rewrite the plant's DNA
Its Ti plasmid transfers T-DNA directly into the plant's chromosomes
It replaces the plant's chloroplasts with modified bacterial ones
